scope: Quantitative written refinement of the already stated physical pure-state polygon zero-support argument. This is an author audit, not a new input-family theorem or a general proof of the harmonic inequality.
notation: For sigma=tilde(rho) in its actual local majority bases, p_i are local minority probabilities, s=sum p_i, P_x are SAME-state computational probabilities, and bar(i) is the word with 0 at i and 1 at all other sites.
identity_and_inequality: Let N_bar_i count minority bits outside i. Pure-state Schmidt duality gives Pr(N_bar_i>=1)>=p_i, since the all-majority probability is at most the complementary marginal's largest eigenvalue 1-p_i. Therefore s-2p_i=sum_{j!=i}p_j-p_i >= E[N_bar_i]-Pr(N_bar_i>=1)=E[(N_bar_i-1)_+] >= 2(P_bar_i+P_1111). Every term is from the same actual pure sigma; no independent marginals or probabilities are substituted.
zero_case: If s-2p_i=0 then both P_bar_i and P_1111 are exactly zero, hence the zero diagonal Schur direction has zero sigma amplitude and the q4 term also vanishes. This strengthens the zero-support observation in 121 without changing its theorem. At positive denominator, P_bar_i/(s-2p_i)<=1/2 and P_1111/(s-2p_i)<=1/2.
continuity_qualification: The quantitative inequality bounds a positive-denominator ratio but does not prove that P_bar_i/(s-2p_i) tends to zero, or that W is continuous, when both numerator and denominator tend to zero. The exact boundary argument in 121 treats the zero directions directly by their actual vanishing amplitudes and pseudoinverse; no limit or denominator cancellation should be silently substituted.
independence_and_process: No new state class, channel claim, numerical proof or independent review is asserted. Earlier errata 125,127,128,130,133 and separate owner cadence finding 132 remain binding under the parent's prospective source-order decision. The 121/123 candidates remain unreviewed.
